newsitem.title: USA: Cavalier Homes to buy Belmont Homes for $77.4 million.
newsitem.headline: Cavalier Homes to buy Belmont Homes for $77.4 million.

text.p: Mobile home maker Cavalier Homes Inc. said Thursday it has agreed to acquire Belmont Homes Inc. in a stock deal valued at about $77.4 million.

The definitive agreement, which came just 10 days after the companies announced they were in merger talks, calls for Cavalier to offer 0.8 share of its common stock for each Belmont share in a tax-free pooling of interests.
Cavalier said it will issue about 7.6 million common shares in the deal, giving it a total of about 20 million shares outstanding.
Based on Wednesday's closing prices, the deal values Belmont at about $8.15 per share.
Cavalier's stock was unchanged at $10.19 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading. Belmont edged down 12.5 cents to $7.75 on Nasdaq.
The companies said Barry Donnell will remain chairman of Cavalier, and David Roberson will remain its president and chief executive officer.

Cavalier Chief Executive David Roberson said the transaction is expected to give the mobile home makers a stronger position in a competitive industry that has been suffering from weak pricing and high retail inventories.
"This deal is not based on cost-cutting strategies or the loss of management or personnel," he said.
He also expressed hope that the industry's troubles will be a short-term phenomenon.

"We do not feel like there is a fundamental problem with the ability for the industry to grow over time. We hope this is going to be short-lived, although we cannot predict when it's going to be over," he said.
Cavalier also said the deal is expected to dilute earnings slightly for the rest of 1997 and in 1998.
Cavalier's executive offices will remain in Addison, Ala. Belmont will become a subsidiary of Cavalier, and its headquarters will remain in Belmont, Miss.
Two Belmont directors will be elected to the Cavalier board.
The deal is targeted to close within four months.
The past year has been difficult for both Cavalier and Belmont. In addition to the fundamental industry problems, the chief executives of both companies have died.
